text:
neil: Heads-up — saw a perf regression on the continuous microbatch path in canary this morning. batch formation is collapsing into tiny batches and queue depth shot up. :eyes:
anya: Oof. Any trace that points to kernel switch or kvcache thrash?
neil: There's a correlated spike in kernel selection latencies around 10:01 UTC. KV cache hit-rate dipped ~15% at the same time.
ben: Can you paste the promql you used? I'll pull the dashboard for the canary pool.
neil: grabbed a few queries and a tiny log sample.

ben: ```promql
# batch util and queue depth for canary pool
avg_over_time(redwood_batcher_batch_utilization{pool="canary"}[5m])
max_over_time(redwood_queue_depth{pool="canary"}[5m])

# tokens/sec and kernel select latency
sum by(pool) (rate(redwood_inference_tokens_total[1m]))
avg_over_time(redwood_batcher_kernel_select_latency_ms{pool="canary"}[5m])
```

neil: log snippet: 
```
[2026-03-18T10:01:23Z] batcher: form_batch id=0x7f size=2 tokens=64 kernel=attn_v1 chosen=auto
[2026-03-18T10:01:24Z] batcher: kvcache miss bucket=prefix user=team-x hit_rate=0.62
[2026-03-18T10:01:24Z] runtime: kernel_select took=38ms (fallback to generic)
```

anya: Interesting — kernel_select latency 38ms is high for that model. Could be kernel thrash from rapid alternation between short/long seqs. Did we recently change the routing policy or token-budget steering?
neil: Not on canary config. But a controller change was rolled that tweaks queue soft-cap and token_budget_target for low-priority pools yesterday.
sam: I rolled the soft-cap tweak but only for non-canary. I'll double-check.

ben: Dashboards show batch_util dropping to ~14% for ~3m, queue depth up to 320, tokens/sec down ~25%. KV hit-rate also drops concurrently. Looks like tiny batches + colder KV leads to more kernel fallbacks => throughput loss.
anya: Sounds like an interaction: queue soft-cap change moved waiting heuristics so batches flush earlier, reducing batch size, which reduces prefix reuse -> kvcache ineffective -> kernel_select loses profile and falls back.
neil: Proposed short-term fix: raise the soft-cap for canary pool back to previous and bump token_budget_target by +20% so we tolerate slightly longer waits to form healthier batches. Then watch kvcache/hit-rate and kernel_select latency.
sam: OK will rollback the soft-cap change in 10m and patch the token_budget target.

ben: Creating a tiny dashboard panel for quick triage: batch_size, queue_depth, batch_util, kvcache_hit_rate, kernel_select_p50/p95, tokens_per_sec. Will add an annotation for the controller roll.
neil: Also adding a short sampling probe that logs the kernel chosen + kv hit boolean for 1% of requests so we can correlate at request level without heavy load. Example probe payload: 
```
{ "probe": "batch_sample", "kernel": "attn_v1", "kvcache_hit": true, "batch_size": 8, "latency_ms": 12 }
```

anya: Good. Can we add a Prometheus alert: when batch_util < 20% AND queue_depth > 200 for >2m AND kvcache_hit_rate < 0.7 -> page eng-runtime?
sre-bot: Alert rule created in staging for review: redwood_batching_degradation_canary. Thresholds are editable.

sam: Rollback deployed at 10:12 UTC. Initial metrics already moving: batch_size climbing, kvcache hit_rate recovering.
neil: Great. Leave the probe and dashboard in place; we'll iterate on token_budget steering. Next steps: (1) collect probe data for 6h, (2) run an ablation where we toggle token_budget_target +/- 10%, (3) evaluate kernel_select p95 and tokens/sec changes.
ben: I'll schedule A/B experiments and post a short report in #eng-runtime tomorrow.
anya: Thanks — this feels like a policy-kvcache-kernel feedback loop. If we can surface a combined signal (batch_util * kvcache_hit_rate) to the router we could avoid bad states.
neil: Agreed — long-term idea: router avoids small-batch states when kvcache hit rate below threshold. Filed a ticket: INF-8723.

sam: Ping me if anything regresses after rollback.
neil: Thanks all. :thumbsup:
